source.title: The gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is widening
source.author: albertzeyer

title.zh: LLM能力认知差距正在扩大

excerpt.zh: LLM能力认知差距正在扩大：Karpathy认为，免费用户、专业用户和内部前沿系统访问者看到的是截然不同的AI现实。
excerpt.en: LLM capability is being understood unevenly as free users, professional users, and internal frontier teams see very different AI realities.

text.en: Why LLM capability now looks like a funnel

text.zh: LLM能力的社会认知正在变得更不均衡。Andrej Karpathy在X上的一篇长帖称，围绕大语言模型真实能力的分歧，已经不只是两群人在互相误解，而更像一个陡峭的使用与访问漏斗。
text.en: Public understanding of LLM capability is becoming more uneven. In a long post on X, Andrej Karpathy argued that disagreement about what large language models can actually do is no longer just two groups talking past each other, but closer to a steep funnel of usage and access.

text.zh: 他给出的粗略估算是：约60亿人几乎没有接触过LLM；约10亿至20亿人只是偶尔使用免费版ChatGPT式产品；约2000万人在数学和代码等领域使用前沿级模型；而只有约5000人能接触内部最先进系统。这些数字是他的“餐巾纸估算”，应被视为判断框架，而不是精确统计。
text.en: His rough estimate is that about 6 billion people have barely encountered LLMs, 1 to 2 billion use free ChatGPT-like products casually, about 20 million use frontier-grade models professionally in areas such as math and code, and roughly 5,000 people have access to the most advanced internal systems. These are napkin estimates, so they should be read as a framing device rather than precise statistics.

text.zh: 差距来自任务、领域和访问权限
text.en: The gap comes from tasks, domains, and access

text.zh: Karpathy的核心观点是，体验差异会直接塑造判断。免费层用户可能只看到一个偶尔出错的聊天机器人，把它当作更好的搜索或写作辅助；而在代码、数学等可验证、数字化且经济价值高的任务中，专业用户可能看到代理完成过去需要数周或数月的大型项目。
text.en: Karpathy’s central point is that experience shapes judgment. Free-tier users may see a sometimes awkward chatbot and treat it as a better search box or writing aid. Professional users working in code, math, and other digital, verifiable, economically valuable domains may instead see agents complete large projects that previously took weeks or months.

text.zh: 他还把差距归因于三个因素：任务的野心和周期越大，系统越能显出影响；模型能力具有不平滑的“锯齿状”分布；访问层级从免费、付费到内部系统依次拉开。也就是说，同一个技术浪潮，会在普通消费者、专业开发者和内部研究团队之间呈现完全不同的速度感。
text.en: He attributes the gap to three forces: the impact grows with the ambition and time horizon of the task; model capability is jagged rather than uniform; and access differs across free, paid, and internal tiers. The same technology wave can therefore feel modest to consumers, dramatic to professional developers, and faster still to internal research teams.

text.zh: 最大问题是验证与治理
text.en: The key open question is verification and governance

text.zh: 这篇帖子在Hacker News上引发大量讨论，说明分歧本身已经成为AI采用的一部分。值得注意的是，Karpathy提到的内部能力包括长时间、多代理协作、网络攻防、科学发现和数学推进等场景，但外部世界只能看到有限预览，无法独立确认全部细节。
text.en: The post drew extensive discussion on Hacker News, which shows that disagreement itself has become part of AI adoption. Karpathy mentions internal capabilities such as long-running multi-agent collaboration, cyber offense and defense, scientific discovery, and mathematical progress, but the outside world has only limited previews and cannot independently verify every detail.

text.zh: 因此，最重要的限制不是简单地问“AI有没有用”，而是如何评估不同访问层看到的能力、如何让人类审查跟上机器生成的工作量，以及哪些领域的突破能够被公开复现。认知差距若继续扩大，企业、政策制定者和公众可能会在不同事实基础上讨论同一个技术。
text.en: The important limitation is not simply whether AI is useful. It is how to evaluate capabilities seen at different access levels, how human review can keep pace with machine-generated work, and which breakthroughs can be publicly reproduced. If the understanding gap keeps widening, companies, policymakers, and the public may end up debating the same technology from very different factual baselines.
